Looking at the code, I can see the inconsistency clearly:

- **`__contains__` (line 483)**: uses `self.timer() < link.expires` (item is NOT expired if time < expires)
- **`__iter__` (line 525)**: uses `time < curr.expires` (same logic)
- **`__getitem__` (line 491)**: uses `not (self.timer() < link.expires)` (consistent with above)
- **`expire()` (line 557)**: uses `time > curr.expires` (item IS expired if time > expires)

The bug is in the `expire()` method at line 557. It uses `time > curr.expires` when it should use `not (time < curr.expires)` or equivalently `time >= curr.expires` to be consistent with the boundary condition. 

Actually, looking more carefully: when `time == expires`, the item should be considered expired (the TTL has elapsed). So:
- NOT expired condition: `time < expires`
- IS expired condition: `time >= expires` (not `time > expires`)

The fix is to change line 557 from `time > curr.expires` to `time >= curr.expires`:
